warnings.message: Same full target sentence is reused across multiple scored activities.

manualReview.scope: Model/editor semantic and pedagogy review of Lesson 0099; not an independent human or real-learner test.

englishNaturalness.evidence: “The start is at nine.” and “It is a good start.” are natural short uses of the bounded noun sense.

persianMeaningQuality.evidence: Persian copy consistently renders start as آغاز/شروع in the program context.

pedagogicalClarity.evidence: The single lexical target is first tied to schedule time and then recombined in a simple evaluation.

distractorQuality.evidence: Distractors distinguish the target noun from an opposite meaning and unrelated familiar language.

dialoguePlausibility.evidence: A community program schedule gives a concrete reason to ask about its start.

difficultyFit.evidence: Both learner responses remain short and use familiar A1 frames.

repetitionUsefulness.evidence: start is practiced through recognition, guided dialogue, changed-context transfer and hidden retrieval.

transferQuality.evidence: The second response changes from stating start time to evaluating the beginning.

overallCoherence.evidence: Scenario, dialogue, activities and outcome share the same bounded noun sense.

learnerExperience.evidence: No real learner test is claimed; learner-experience confidence is intentionally limited.

limitations: No independent human or real learner test has been performed.
The review covers only the bounded A1 noun sense.
Generated audio prosody is not evaluated at this text stage.
resolvedFindings: Persian copy preserves the selected meaning.
The final activity requires hidden retrieval.
The community arc returns after 5 Lessons and learner role rotates from Nina to Iris.
